cases.purpose: State directory safety and recovery: refusal of unsafe directories, atomic temp-and-rename writes observed with inotify, lock collision, recovery of stale state left by a SIGKILLed listener (leftover scratch files, a forged listener_pid), and preservation of unrelated files.
cases.oracle: Independent protocol oracle. Persistent candidate shells run the UNCHANGED builtin as uid 2000 in private state directories on IPv4 loopback inside the disposable VM. The wire format (1212-byte datagram, BCLSTR2 magic, big-endian port, 32-row table, keyed BLAKE2b-256 over the first 1180 bytes) is the fixture's own implementation on hashlib, validated in setup against BLAKE2b known answers and round trips; oracle peers, probes and decoys are owned UDP sockets that validate every request field by field. Expected values never come from candidate output alone: identities and rosters are cross-checked on the wire (authenticated PONG and ROSTER packets), file contents are parsed independently, timing bounds come from the documented deadline (request deadline, heartbeat every quarter, expiry after three), and kernel facts come from /proc (process tree, UDP table, receive queues), inotify, bind() collisions, modes and owners. Setup controls (a failure is an ERROR, never a candidate result): hashing and codec known answers, loopback delivery of 0/1/1212/65507 byte datagrams, the UDP table and its queues, wildcard decoys, every oracle peer mode, inotify atomicity detection, and the persistent-shell driver (status/stdout/stderr extraction, deadline kill, removal of a child that outlives its shell, reaping). Only processes started by the fixture are signaled; every key is evaluated for every vector, an unevaluated key prints ERROR, and any control or fixture exception prints CONTROL-INVALID and exits 97.
cases.comparison: Every key of every vector is evaluated and must be yes. [refuse-unsafe-directory] modes-refused: init on directories of mode 0755, 0750, 0705, 0770 and 0777 exits 1 with the private-directory diagnostic and no output; modes-untouched: those directories keep their mode and stay empty (no lock, no state file); symlink-refused: a symlink to a private directory is refused (lstat sees a link); symlink-untouched: the link target stays empty and the link remains; file-refused: a regular file in place of the directory is refused; file-untouched: the file keeps its bytes; not-owned-refused: a root-owned directory without group/other bits is refused (ownership branch); not-owned-untouched: that directory keeps inode, mode, owner and mtime; join-refused: join into a 0755 directory is refused with the same diagnostic and creates nothing; join-no-traffic: the refused join sent no datagram to its seed endpoint; no-listener-started: no listener child exists in the shell after all refusals; private-accepted: a pre-created 0700 directory with unrelated files is accepted, a listener starts, unrelated files stay. [atomic-state-writes] init-status: init with a fixture key succeeds; watch-captured: inotify saw the lock creation and a rename into place of every state file; final-names-by-rename: no state file name was ever created, modified or closed for writing in place; each appeared by rename; scratch-then-rename: each rename source is the file's own .NAME.tmp, created and closed for writing before the rename; no-scratch-left: no .tmp scratch file remains; roster-replaced-atomically: members was renamed into place at init, at a join and at a leave and never written in place; files-private: every state file is a regular 0600 file. [lock-collision] first-started: the first init succeeds; second-shell-refused: init from a second shell on the same directory exits 1 with the lock diagnostic; same-shell-refused: init again from the owning shell is refused the same way; state-unchanged: the directory snapshot (inodes, mtimes, digests) is unchanged by the refusals; first-listener-alive: the first listener is still alive; first-listener-serves: an authenticated PING still gets a valid PONG; no-second-listener: the second shell owns no child and the first shell exactly its one listener. [stale-recovery-leave] setup-stale: a listener was SIGKILLed leaving state files; stale-status-stopped: status reports state=stopped with the stale cluster id; leave-status: leave exits 0 printing left cluster; state-files-removed: all seven state files are gone; scratch-removed: the leftover .members.tmp, .state.tmp and .cluster_id.tmp are gone; lock-and-unrelated-kept: lock remains and every unrelated entry is unchanged (inode, mode, mtime, digest, link target); forged-pid-not-signaled: the owned sentinel named in the forged listener_pid file is still alive; status-uninitialized: status then reports state=uninitialized. [stale-recovery-init] setup-stale: a listener was SIGKILLed leaving state files; init-status: init on the stale directory succeeds; ids-regenerated: the node id and cluster id differ from the stale ones; scratch-removed: the leftover scratch files are gone; unrelated-kept: unrelated entries are unchanged; forged-pid-not-signaled: the sentinel named in the forged listener_pid file is still alive; status-initialized: status reports state=initialized with the new listener pid; serves-after-recovery: the recovered listener answers an authenticated PING. [symlinked-state-names] init-status: init succeeds with symlinks standing at members, private_key and .cluster_id.tmp; target-unchanged: the symlink target file is unchanged; names-replaced-by-files: members and private_key are now regular files and private_key holds the supplied key; scratch-link-removed: the scratch symlink was removed, not followed. Retained in the case tree: observations.jsonl (every command with its raw stdout, stderr, status, duration and finish time, every oracle exchange as hex, teardown findings, and r2 trace: the ordered observation timeline per vector - every datagram sent and received as hex with the source port, every peer verdict, inotify events, /proc process and UDP table observations, bind probes, directory snapshots, file contents read, kills, sentinel states, and every key evaluation interleaved with the observations that produced it) and the state directories themselves; the setup report is the stdout of the setup step.

cases.purpose: Ping by node id and by numeric loopback endpoint against an owned oracle peer: the request has the documented size, magic, type, identity, fresh nonce and valid keyed MAC; unknown nodes send nothing; silent and non-protocol replies end in a bounded timeout failure.

[ping-resolution] by-node: ping NODE resolves the roster row and prints ok NODE (three times); by-endpoint: ping 127.0.0.1:PORT prints ok with that endpoint (three times); requests-received: the oracle peer received exactly six requests; request-size: every request is exactly 1212 bytes; request-header: every request has the BCLSTR2 magic, type PING and count 0; request-identity: every request carries the state cluster id, node id and port; request-rows-zero: the row table of every request is all zero; request-mac: every request MAC verifies under the group key; nonces-fresh: the six nonces are pairwise different and not zero; request-source: requests come from 127.0.0.1 and an ephemeral port other than the listener ports. [ping-unknown-node] status: ping of unknown node ids (and an upper-cased real id) exits 1 without output; message: each prints the unknown node diagnostic with the target; nothing-sent: neither the oracle peer nor the own-port decoy received a datagram.
